network_card.title: The pot your knives are prepping for
network_card.description: Our sister site compares dutch ovens the same way: enameled against bare cast iron, how the lid seals, real oven-safe limits, and which size fits the way you cook.

articles.title: The Best Kitchen Knife Sets Under $100
articles.description: Under a hundred dollars you can still get forged steel, full tang and a published contents list. Three that deliver, and the claims to ignore.

articles.title: Stamped vs Forged Kitchen Knives: Which Should You Buy?
articles.description: One is hammered from a bar of steel, the other cut from a sheet. The difference is in the hand, not in the edge — and the cheaper one is not worse.

articles.title: How Many Kitchen Knives Do You Actually Need?
articles.description: Three, and the third is arguable. What a 15-piece block really contains, and why the piece count is the worst way to compare two sets.

articles.title: The Best Japanese-Style Knife Sets
articles.description: A gyutou is ground near 15 degrees where a German knife sits around 20. That narrower edge bites more easily and forgives less. Three sets worth the attention.

articles.title: Knife Sets With a Built-In Sharpener: Worth It?
articles.description: A sharpener in the block touches up the edge every time you put the knife away. Genuinely useful, and not the same as sharpening properly.

articles.title: How to Keep a Knife Set Sharp for Years
articles.description: Nothing here is difficult and all of it is skipped. The washing, the storing and the sharpening that separate a set that lasts from one replaced in two years.

articles.title: The Best Knife Sets for a First Apartment
articles.description: A complete kitchen for the price of one good knife. What to accept at this price, what never to accept, and the three sets that get it right.

articles.title: What Is Actually in a 15-Piece Knife Set?
articles.description: Eight knives, six steak knives and a block — or seven knives, shears, a sharpener and a block. Two sets with the same number can be very different purchases.

articles.title: The Best Knife Sets Without a Block
articles.description: A block is furniture. If your counter is short or your drawer is deep, these are the sets that give you blades instead of a box.

articles.title: German vs Japanese Kitchen Knives
articles.description: Heavier and more forgiving, or lighter and sharper. Both are right — the question is what you cook and how carefully you treat your knives.

articles.title: The Best Knife Sets to Give as a Gift
articles.description: A knife set is a gift people keep for a decade or resent for a month. What makes one a good present, and the three that are.

articles.title: What Rockwell Hardness Tells You About a Knife
articles.description: 56 plus or minus 2 appears on good listings and nowhere else. What the number measures, what it trades, and why mid-fifties is the sensible place to be.

articles.title: The Best Steak Knife Sets
articles.description: Six steak knives come free in most blocks and most of them are poor. When buying them separately makes sense, and what to look for.

articles.title: How to Choose a Kitchen Knife Set
articles.description: Six questions in the order that matters. Answer them and the shortlist writes itself — and the piece count is not one of them.

articles.title: The Best Splurge-Worthy Knife Sets
articles.description: Above a hundred and fifty dollars the pitch changes: more steel, a sharpening mechanism built into the block, twenty pieces instead of fifteen. What actually justifies the price, and three sets that earn it.

articles.title: "Dishwasher Safe" Knife Sets: What the Label Actually Means
articles.description: Three listings in this catalogue print the words dishwasher safe on a set of kitchen knives. The dishwasher will still dull the edge. What the label is actually protecting against.

articles.title: What 'Full Tang' Actually Means on a Knife Set
articles.description: The metal does not stop at the blade. On a full-tang knife it runs the length of the handle, riveted through — and you can usually see it without reading a single spec.
